newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Residues an issue for Australian wool - IWS.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Residues an issue for Australian wool - IWS.

text.p: Australian woolgrowers would require accurate market signals from customers before major changes in chemical usage patterns occur on-farm, the International Wool Secretariat (IWS) said in a statement.
This was shown in a survey of growers' attitudes conducted in conjunction with Monash University, IWS said.
The survey showed woolgrowers believed the issue of chemical residues was a major and important issue facing the Australian industry but needed more detailed answers to effect change.

Australian wool had the reputation of being the cleanest in the world, but growers were being called to arms once more to lower residue levels further as customers increasingly demanded a cleaner product, IWS national coordinator of chemical residues Peter Hanrahan said.
IWS and the wool industry had embarked on an education campaign to assist woolgrowers in reducing residue levels in the clip, he said.
